title: Issue 1 Cover — At the Municipal Temporal Displacement Integration Department
summary: Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar sit in an aggressively ordinary municipal waiting room. The joke is rigid bureaucracy surrounding three people who have already been waiting long enough for waiting itself to become the activity.
settingText: Municipal Department of Temporal Displacement Integration waiting room, present-day New York: pale civic walls, molded chairs, institutional floor tile and fluorescent ceiling panels.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — SEATED HORIZONTAL TRIPTYCH. Broad, frontal and almost embarrassingly static beneath the fixed municipal masthead.

Carrie sits left with clipboard and coffee. Bjorn sits centered, hands clasped, physically heavy and contained. Gunnar sits right with queue slips and shield. Preserve their exact canonical faces, builds, hair, clothing and distinguishing details.
The three should feel as though they have already been waiting long enough for waiting itself to become the activity. Their expressions are contained and specific, not posed or heroic.
Let molded chairs, fluorescent ceiling panels, pale walls and institutional floor tile create the contradiction. Keep the environment ordinary and materially believable.
Background citizens are few, quiet and visually subordinate. Nobody is fascinated by the three leads.

Redraw the scene in Vikings 2026's established painted-comic language: clearly illustrated faces and surfaces, controlled texture, tactile civic materials, no photographic skin, lens effects, bokeh, prestige-TV rendering or cinematic color grading.
The Issue 1 reference controls trade dress only. Preserve the strong seated composition while treating the illustration beneath the masthead as a new production image.
No fantasy masthead, runes, parchment, Viking typography, decorative shields, heroic lighting or faux-medieval graphic motifs.

directionInline.text: Keep the humor dry and institutional. The visual mass of the three seated figures should be as rigid as the bureaucracy above them.

title: Issue 2 Cover — Landfall Bushwick
summary: The household has shelter, but reaching it feels like an expedition: six historical figures climb an absurd number of ordinary Bushwick stairs with their possessions.
settingText: Narrow Bushwick apartment stairwell at night, rising through repeated flights and landings toward the fifth-floor corridor and apartment.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — STEEP DIAGONAL ASCENT. Treat the stairwell like a vertical dungeon crawl without making the building sinister.

Distribute the six historical figures across multiple elevations and turns rather than lining them up on one flight. One person looks toward the next landing, another glances backward, one pauses under a bundle, and another squeezes around a railing turn.

Bjorn remains serious about the destination but is visibly tired. Gunnar is visibly calculating how many more flights there could possibly be. The household is genuinely pleased to have shelter; the climb is simply much more of an expedition than expected.
Bundled possessions should make the climb physical without turning the scene into misery. Keep the household active, capable and weary.
The top-floor architecture must be physically coherent: stair flight to landing, landing to corridor, corridor to apartment door. Do not place a door impossibly against the stair geometry.
The door and brass key are incidental destination details, not the focal hook. The dominant read is the party climbing through repeated vertical geometry.
A neighbor is optional. If present, keep them tiny and incidental so the household and upward motion remain the cover.
Use ordinary Bushwick materials—painted railings, worn plaster, practical fixtures, old stairs—without gothic treatment or fantasy atmosphere.

directionInline.text: The cover should feel weary, relieved and faintly absurd rather than defeated. Preserve strong upward progress and distinct body behavior for each household member.

title: Issue 3 Cover — Territory
summary: Gunnar is very small in an enormous unfamiliar city, but his feet are finally on dry land and he can begin solving where he is.
settingText: Bushwick rooftop at dawn, with neighborhood rooflines, street corridors, shadows, water towers, antennas and receding blocks.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — LONE FIGURE AND LARGE NEGATIVE SPACE. Gunnar stands alone near the parapet, physically grounded and intent, much smaller in frame than a conventional heroic cover would make him.

The city reads primarily as neighborhood geometry: rooflines, street corridors, shadows, water towers, antennas and receding blocks. Manhattan may appear only as a distant geographically appropriate feature and must not dominate.
Dawn light comes from the correct eastern side of the city. Do not place the rising sun over Manhattan from Bushwick. Use one useful shadow, roofline or alignment Gunnar can actually study.
Gunnar is orienting himself inside New York, not conquering it. His posture is practical observation, not victory, mysticism or revelation.
The broad sky and geometric city field should make his scale emotionally legible: humility without helplessness.
A tiny neighboring resident doing an ordinary morning task is optional only if it does not weaken the solitude.
No mystical sunrise, fantasy compass motif, glowing map, heroic-overlook pose or Manhattan-as-destiny composition.

directionInline.text: Keep early light beautiful but physically plausible. The cover's power comes from scale, solitude and a navigator turning ordinary city geometry into usable information.

title: Issue 4 Cover — The Iron Worm
summary: Carrie understands the subway as transit. Bjorn and Gunnar have not yet agreed that entering it is sensible.
settingText: New York City subway platform with a northbound train arriving from depth under practical fluorescent light.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — TRAIN / PLATFORM SPLIT. The northbound stainless-steel train occupies the left side as a heavy moving wedge; the platform occupies the right.
Carrie is already positioned naturally for boarding. Bjorn and Gunnar remain just behind or beside her, giving the arriving machine the serious physical assessment it deserves.
Let lit windows, stainless steel, tunnel depth and motion make the train enormous without turning it into a monster. The real object is strange enough.
Keep the three leads and the train in clean silhouette. Remove foreground commuter heads entirely.
Background riders may exist farther down the platform only where they support scale and normal transit behavior. Nobody visibly reacts to the Vikings.
Keep signage minimal and subordinate; do not overload the platform with readable text.
This cover visually bookends Issue 2: old infrastructure forces a laborious climb upward; modern infrastructure offers a machine that carries people underground.
No literal iron-worm creature imagery, foreground observer, reaction crowd or fantasy metaphor.

directionInline.text: Simplify aggressively: train, Carrie, Bjorn, Gunnar, platform edge and tunnel are enough.

title: Issue 5 Cover — The Neighborhood
summary: Bjorn receives his first over-sweet coffee and evaluates the bright steaming cup with the seriousness he would give any questionable foreign substance.
settingText: Bushwick sidewalk coffee cart at morning rush, framed tightly at counter height.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — TIGHT COUNTER TRANSACTION. Use a counter-height or slightly low three-quarter view focused on Bjorn, the bright steaming cup and the vendor.
Bjorn dominates with the cup. His reaction is restrained: inspection, suspicion and perhaps the smallest disapproving expression rather than broad comedy.
The vendor continues working as though this is simply a customer deciding whether he likes his coffee. Do not make the vendor grin at the Viking or perform for the moment.
Gunnar is present but secondary, behind Bjorn in line or just outside the tight primary exchange.
Simplify the cart: steam, stainless steel, stacked cups and one suggestion of breakfast food. Do not render a catalog of pastries, utensils or signs.
Weapon visibility is minimal. The transaction, not Viking equipment, is the image.
Keep the surrounding street fragment subordinate so the cover reads cup + Bjorn + vendor before anything else.
No lifestyle-photography street tableau, cluttered menu text or cart detail competing with the coffee.

directionInline.text: The comedy is intimate and behavioral. Preserve Bjorn's seriousness and the vendor's routine professionalism.

title: Issue 6 Cover — The Tally of Dishonor
summary: Bjorn encounters the institution that supposedly guards and accumulates wealth. It is disappointingly just a neighborhood bank.
settingText: Mundane neighborhood bank branch interior: fluorescent panels, cheap carpet or tile, queue stanchions, desks, teller counter, brochure rack and ordinary security glass.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — FLAT INSTITUTIONAL SYMMETRY. Let a bland rectangular bank interior visually swallow Bjorn.

Bjorn stands inside or just beyond the entrance studying the branch with sincere analytical disappointment. His mental model involves physical custody and defensible wealth; the actual room is people filling forms while tellers click through computers.
Keep the bank visually boring: fluorescent panels, cheap carpet or tile, queue stanchions, ordinary desks, teller counter, brochure rack and practical security glass where appropriate.
No visible vault, treasure, piles of currency, luxurious architecture, glowing screens or aura of financial power.
Carrie may already be moving toward the appointment. Gunnar may independently inspect another piece of the system, but neither should turn the image into an ensemble tableau.
The branch should almost visually underperform beside Bjorn's historical gravity. That contrast is the cover.
Background customers and staff remain routine and sparse. Do not make reflections or abstract invisible-value metaphors the main concept.
No invented bank advertising copy or promotional signage.

directionInline.text: Make the institution more ordinary, not more metaphorical. Flatness and underwhelming civic-commercial function are the graphic joke.

title: Issue 7 Cover — The Skaldic Interface
summary: For once, the modern institution exceeds expectations: Gunnar confronts a physical quantity of accumulated written memory large enough to change what preservation means.
settingText: Grand but recognizably public New York library interior with tall shelving, mezzanine or balcony, reading tables and deep civic architecture.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — SOARING VERTICAL LIBRARY VOLUME. Use tall shelving, a mezzanine, balcony, long reading room or older civic-library proportions to create genuine architectural scale.
Gunnar is the emotional center, standing nearly empty-handed and absorbing the quantity of preserved written memory. His gaze should be drawn upward and inward.
Bjorn is smaller and secondary, already beginning to engage with the collection rather than posing beside Gunnar.
Ordinary readers use tables, shelves and carts without ceremony. Their routine behavior increases the wonder because this enormous archive is normal civic infrastructure to them.
The architecture may be beautiful and grand, but it remains a public institution rather than fantasy architecture.
Do not stage a foreground Viking carrying a comic stack of books. Let volume, height and depth do the work.
Keep category signage minimal and non-dominant.
No glowing books, runes, magical light or exaggerated fantasy-library motifs.

directionInline.text: This issue's institution should feel like a triumph. Architecture and scale, not a prop gag, carry the cover.

title: Issue 8 Cover — Provision
summary: It is a beautiful spring day. New Yorkers see a park; Bjorn and Gunnar see land, weather, food and the next winter.
settingText: Modest Bushwick public park or green on a pleasant April day, with broad usable grass, budding trees and open spring sky.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — LOW PARK / PICNIC COMPOSITION. Use a blanket-level foreground opening into broad green public space and active spring sky.
Carrie, Bjorn and Gunnar occupy a blanket or small patch of grass. A simple spit with meat roasting may make their material relationship with food immediately legible.
Bjorn and Gunnar quietly study soil, new growth, tree buds, available land, weather and supplies. Carrie behaves like someone enjoying or enduring an ordinary park morning.

Around them, ordinary spring leisure continues loosely and peripherally: a frisbee, small recreational drone, reader, dog walker or person lounging in the sun. Keep these actions sparse rather than building a crowd.
The day is unmistakably pleasant April weather. Their seriousness is funny because the conditions are so forgiving.
Give the park enough visual space that the available land itself feels materially useful from their point of view.
No bus-stop staging. Do not show planting, winter weather, storm foreshadowing, survival panic or neighbors laughing at them.

directionInline.text: Sell the collision between recreation and provisioning. Fresh spring openness should dominate the color and space.

title: Issue 9 Cover — Trial of Toil
summary: Bjorn enters an ordinary temporal-displacement support group and finds people from different lost worlds sharing the same unimpressive circle of folding chairs.
settingText: Plain municipal or nonprofit multipurpose meeting room with folding or stackable chairs in a circle, institutional floor, coffee urn, paper cups and tables against the wall.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — CIRCULAR SUPPORT-GROUP COMPOSITION. Build the cover around an imperfect chair circle with a strong empty neutral center.
Bjorn sits as one participant among other displaced people. He remains physically formidable but emotionally contained; he is neither mocked nor giving a heroic speech.

Use the established Group Facilitator and 1987 Participant exactly from their current canonical references. Any additional displaced participants must come from established approved support-group reference pixels; do not invent generic historical gag characters. If those references are unavailable at generation time, crop or limit the circle rather than inventing identities.

The visual comedy comes from radically different historical identities sharing the same unimpressive room: stackable chairs, institutional carpet or tile, coffee urn, paper cups and tables pushed against the wall.
Keep the facilitator on the same kind of chair as everyone else; there is no head position or clinical hierarchy.
The empty center of the chair circle is the major negative-space shape. Let bodies and chair backs create the graphic ring.
Do not reveal Bjorn's later admission about protection, resolve his problem, stage a breakdown or make any participant a gag character.
Move completely away from Apartment 5B and away from household-ensemble cover staging.

directionInline.text: The room should be visually unimpressive enough that the range of displaced identities becomes the entire image.

title: Issue 10 Cover — Belonging
summary: The household remains visibly strange, but the block recognizes them now. Belonging appears through ordinary repeated movement rather than a group portrait.
settingText: Long view down a familiar Bushwick sidewalk with repeating stoops, storefront edges, street trees and building entrances.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — DISTRIBUTED DEPTH ALONG ONE NEIGHBORHOOD BLOCK. Use a long sidewalk view with strong recession rather than a clustered household ensemble.
Distribute members of the household at different depths along the same block, each engaged in an ordinary neighborhood movement. Do not pose all six together.

Recognition happens through small habitual gestures: a neighbor already holds a door because they know someone is coming; a person on a stoop gives a casual greeting; a familiar worker acknowledges one of them without stopping.
Nobody's face says 'look, a Viking.' The household remains visually unmistakable; what has changed is the social meaning of being seen.
Carrie need not dominate. If present, she simply passes through the block as another known person.
Let the neighborhood itself be the connective tissue. No single interaction needs to explain the title.
Keep environmental text minimal and non-readable unless required by continuity.
No sentimental group portrait, neighborhood celebration, welcome party, simultaneous-departure tableau or callback montage.

directionInline.text: Routine recognition, spatial depth and repeated local geography should carry the feeling of belonging without sentimental staging.

title: Issue 11 Cover — War Council
summary: The title is grand; the problem is dull official paperwork. Six lives occupy one domestic table without becoming a unified command staff.
settingText: Apartment 5B table at night, warm and domestic, with a plain official review notice and ordinary household objects.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — OVERHEAD TABLE GEOMETRY. Use a near-overhead view with the dull official review notice close to geometric center.
Carrie, Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and the two male Kin occupy clearly distinct physical territories around the table rather than leaning inward as one command staff.
Separate them through hands, posture and personal objects: mug, fabric, practical tool, key, book or folder. These are signs of six lives, not evidence exhibits.
Carrie's official folder sits at an edge and looks visually smaller than the accumulated life around the table.
The room remains warm, domestic and unheroic. The title WAR COUNCIL supplies all necessary grandeur.
The notice itself is visually boring: plain paper and ordinary municipal formatting, without ominous stamps, seals or thriller treatment.
No maps, weapons, tactical posing, dramatic spotlighting or medieval council imagery.
Preserve clean top-down graphic stillness rather than 'everyone huddles over strategy.'

directionInline.text: The table should read as six separate people sharing space around one absurdly dull sheet of paper.

title: Issue 12 Cover — Trial by Combat
summary: Bjorn has come to face institutional judgment. Of course he wore armor.
settingText: Municipal hearing-center security checkpoint and fluorescent corridor, morning, with metal-detector arch and adjacent X-ray scanner/conveyor.
panelPlan: GRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE — DEAD-CENTER SECURITY ARCH / SEVERE FRONTAL SYMMETRY. Frame canonical Bjorn squarely inside the rectangular detector arch, facing the reader directly.
Bjorn wears his established armor. His expression is composed, sincere and absolutely nonaggressive. He is not in a battle stance.
His weapons have already been surrendered and are visibly moving through or resting on the adjacent X-ray scanner/conveyor. Their presence is procedural, not threatening; nothing is held or raised.
A security officer handles the next checkpoint step with ordinary professional concentration. The building contributes nothing heroic.
Carrie waits to one side with her folder. Gunnar, Astrid and the two male Kin remain farther back as separate applicants rather than Bjorn's retinue.
Other visitors may remove belts, empty pockets or stare at paperwork without caring that an armored ninth-century man is ahead of them. Keep them secondary and do not clutter the symmetry.
The detector arch functions visually like a ceremonial gate only because Bjorn makes it look like one. The fluorescent corridor remains painfully mundane.
No judges, gavels, flames, triumphant imagery, drawn weapons, raised shields, fantasy symbolism or battle-poster staging.

directionInline.text: Make this the cleanest, most iconic cover of the run: frontal, symmetric, procedural and visually severe.
